newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen stock eases as takeover fever ebbs.
newsitem.headline: Loewen stock eases as takeover fever ebbs.

text.p: Loewen Group Inc stock sank further on Monday on expectations that its battle with hostile bidder Service Corp International would likely last months, traders said.
Loewen shares were down 7/8 at 39-7/8 in New York, while Service stock gained 3/8 to 30-3/8.

Loewen, North America's second biggest funeral home operator, has not responded to Service's US$45 a share bid announced last week. But the vehemence of its earlier rejection of a US$43 a share offer has generated widespread expectations that it will spurn the sweetened bid too.

After soaring in mid-September on Service's first offer, Loewen shares began sliding late last week on profit-taking and selling by arbitragers. Although many traders believe Loewen may yet succumb to Service, they said it could take many months.
"This could be a three, four or five month process. A lot of people have gotten out (of the stock) to see how it plays out, with an idea maybe they will get back in later on," said one trader.
Added an analyst: "The arbs are not in this right now. It's going to be a slow process in which Service Corp is going to try to increase the pressure on Loewen."
